Thanks Markus — that list looks right. A few clarifications from our security team: 

1) Primary ask: a sample of the access/audit log for the last 30 days showing the following columns: timestamp, actor_id (internal/external), actor_type (API key/user/service), action (inference, admin:update, model:deploy, key:rotate), resource_id (model, dataset, route), outcome (success/fail), ip_address, session_id, token_id (hashed ok).

2) Delivery: preferred sent to our S3 staging bucket (s3://bh-security-uploads) via a pre-signed URL. Drive link is ok for initial review but S3 is our compliance workflow.

3) Retention: we need to know Redwood's default retention for audit logs and options for 13/24/36 month retention. Also whether we can configure shorter retention per-tenant.

4) PII: confirm whether PII fields (email, client-provided PII in model input) are present in logs by default; we require a redaction option before export.

5) Export formats: CSV and newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) are both acceptable; parquet preferred for large exports.

We can review the sample internally and then set up a technical deep-dive (security + infra) next week if the sample looks complete.

Hi Elaine — thanks for the detailed list. We've prepared a small package and uploaded the sample artifacts: 

- redwood-audit-sample-202603.csv (5 rows) — columns: timestamp, actor_id, actor_type, action, resource_id, outcome, ip_address, session_id, token_hash, model_hash
- redwood-audit-sample-202603.ndjson (5 objects) — same fields in ndjson format
- access-export-schema.json — JSON schema for all supported fields and types
- README_redaction.md — brief explanation of redaction options and default behaviour

Notes / answers: 
- Default retention: 12 months for audit logs in Hosted; Dedicated/Private customers can request configurable retention up to 36 months. We support per-tenant retention policies for Dedicated/Private.
- PII handling: by default we log IP addresses and actor identifiers. We do not store raw model inputs in the audit log by default (only metadata and model output hashes). Customers can enable optional input-logging; if enabled we provide a redaction pipeline to remove emails and obvious PII via regex and ML detectors before export.
- Export formats: we provide CSV, ndjson, Parquet, and direct S3 export via pre-signed URLs. For very large exports we recommend Parquet with an S3 transfer.
- Session/token ids: we include hashed token/session identifiers; we can provide salted hashes on request for cross-system correlation under NDA.
- Compliance evidence: we can produce a time-ordered access list (who/what/when) and a signed manifest for audit purposes.

Delivery: sample files are available here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B-example-log-samples (temporary review). If Blue Horizon confirms S3, Markus please provide the presigned URL and we'll push a production-ready export there.

If the security team is happy with the sample, let's book the technical deep-dive next Tuesday 4/20 — 45 minutes (ops + infra + product).

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
